correctness.rationale: The Euler factors are 1+p^(−3a) at a present prime. Defant Lemma 2.2 gives p_(j+1)^3<2p_j^3 for j>=10; the decreasing log(1+x)/x then gives w_j<2w_(j+1). Any failure w_j>S_j propagates, whereas the primes in (p_j,2p_j] make S_j/w_j tend to infinity by the prime number theorem. The remaining j=5..9 inequalities are finite. The greedy residual lies between zero and the remaining log-tail under either choice, yielding every point of [1,T] in the squarefree closure; higher exponents cannot enlarge this interval. The bound 1+p^(−3A_p)<=T makes the intervals for exponent 0 and A_p overlap, covering every higher exponent interval, also after scaling by any fixed other factors. Thus the finite union is exact. With common multiplier T on the right, sorted consecutive starting values x_i split components exactly where x_(i+1)/x_i>T. The independent rational replay with Q=2000 verified all five small-prime inequalities, four caps, all 134 consecutive comparisons, and all fourteen table rows and label counts, giving thirteen strict gaps; the common right-end multiplier exceeds 1.
residual_risks: The exact rational checks do not supply the prime number theorem or Defant's infinite prime-ratio bound. The result applies only at t=−3.

evidence: Defant's threshold eta* is about 1.974255. The finite criterion for 1<r<=3 uses m in {1,2,3,4,6,9}; §3 treats component-count questions as further work. Zubrilina studies ordinary sigma.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general threshold and finite inequalities decide only connectedness. For ordinary sigma, the local factor includes all intermediate prime powers; even a general component algorithm for it is not a theorem about the unitary closure. Exact coverage here is furnished by the separate unitary records, not by those publications.
